questions.question: Backup server init request to backup client. Backup server init request to backup client. This request instructs the backup client to send its metadata to backup server and the data to be backed up to the appropriate storage node. On receiving this request, backup client sends the metadata to the backup server. Backup server writes this metadata on its metadata catalog. Backup client also sends the data to the storage node and storage node writes the data to the storage device. After all the data is backed up, the storage node closes the connection to the backup device. Backup server writes backup completion status to the metadata catalog. Backup s/w provides reporting capabilities based on backup catalog and log files. They include info such as amount of data backed up, no. of completed backups, no. of incompleted backups, types of errors while backing etc. 2 Marks 2 Marks .Physical Tape library: -Provides housing and power for a no of tape drives and tape cartridges along with robotic arm (Picker mech.).Backup s/w has intelligence to manage the robotic arm and entire backup process. -Tape drives RD/WR data from and to a tape. -Tape cartridges are placed in the slots when not in use. -Robotic arms are used move tapes around the library. -Each physical component in a tape library has an individual element address, used as an addressing mechanism. -It is necessary to ensure that the tape drive is kept busy continuously to prevent the gaps between the blocks. -Gaps can be eliminated by buffering the data on the tape drive or by adjusting speed of the tape drive to match data transfer rate. 1 Mark

questions.question: Cache vaulting Cache is exposed to the risk of uncommitted data loss due to power failure. To solve problem: Powering the memory ….. In the event of extended power failure, large amount of data may not be committed HENCE, STORAGE VENDORS USE A SET OF PHYSICAL DISKS TO DUMP THE CONTENTS OF CACHE DURING POWER FAILURE. questions.question: Little’s Law: Describes the relationship between the number of requests in a queue and the response time. N=a×R “N” is the total number of requests in the queuing system “a” is the arrival rate “R” is the average response time (or TAT i.e. time from arrival to departure from system) Utilization law: Defines the I/O controller utilization U = a × Rs “U” is the I/O controller utilization 2 Marks “RS“ is the service time Arrival 6 5 4 3 2 1 I/ Controller O black box: consisting of two elements: Queue: Loc. where the I/O requests wait before it is processed by the I/O controller. Disk I/O controller: Processes I/Os that are waiting in the queue one by one. Arrival rate: Rate at which I/O requests arrive at the controller (Generated by the application) Arrival rate, queue length and time taken by the I/O controller to process each request det the performance of the disk system. Utilization of I/O controller (U= a × Rs) Total response time (R=Rs /1-U) But Ra=1/a U=Rs/Ra S=service rate-arrival rate And R = 1/ (service rate-arrival rate) On simplifying Hence Average response time = R= Rs / (1-U) Number of requests in a queue NQ = Number requests in the system N -Number od requests on the controller NQ = N - U =aXR-U = aX (Rs /(1-U)) - U On simplifying Average queue size = U2 / (1-U) Time spent by a request in the queue = time spent by a request in the system OR avg response time - the time spent on the controller = Rs / (1-U) - Rs On simplifying Time spent by a request in the queue = U x R 3 Marks 2A. HOT SPARE refers to a spare HDD in a RAID set that temporarily replaces a failed HDD of a RAID set. Hot spare takes the identity of the failed HDD in the array. Methods of data recovery depending on RAID impl: -If parity RAID is used, then the data is rebuilt onto the hot spare from the parity and the data on the surviving HDDs in the surviving set. -If mirroring is used, then the data from the surviving mirror is used to copy the data. When failed HDD is replaced with a new HDD, one of the following takes place: -Hot spare replaces new HDD permanently. i.e. it is no longer a hot spare, and a new hot spare is added to the array. -When a new HDD is added to the system, data from the hot spare is copied to it. The hot spare returns to its idle state, ready to replace the next failed drive. 2 Marks DISK LOAD IN RAID 5: =0.6 × 5,200+4x(0.4 × 5,200) [B,ze the write penalty for RAID 5 is 4] =11,440 IOPS DISK LOAD IN RAID 1: =0.6 × 5,200+2x(0.4 × 5,200) [B,ze the write penalty for RAID 1 is 2] =7,280 IOPS 2 Marks The computed diskload determines the no of disk required for application. If an HDD with a specification of a maximum 180 IOPS for the application, the no of disks required to meet the workload for the RAID will be RAID5: 11,440 / 180 = 64 disks RAID 1: 7,280 / 180 = 42 disks (Nearest Even no.) 1 Marks

questions.subject: local:information-storage-and-management
questions.question: Application Programming Interface (API) Application Programming Interface (API) -A high level implementation that specifies how clients can make service requests. -A set of function calls that enables communication. Binary large object (BLOB) -The actual data without the descriptive info. The user data represents the actual content of a file and is independent of the filename and physical location. C-Clip -A package containing the user's data and associated metadata C-Clip ID (C-Clip handle or C-Clip reference) is the CA that the system returns to the client application. Content Address (CA) -Hash algorithm creates the content address/ object address. -Hash algo considers all aspects of the content while generating CA to the user application. A unique number is calculated from the sequence of bits of the file content. -An identifier that uniquely addresses the content of a file and not its location. Unlike location-based addresses, content addresses are inherently stable and, once calculated, they never change and always refer to the same content. -The hash output or digest is a type of fingerprint and is used to locate the file in CAS. -When a user tries to retrieve a file, server sends the CA to CAS with appropriate fn to read the file. CAS uses CA to locate the file and passes it back to the application server. C-Clip Descriptor File (CDF) An XML file that the system creates when making a C-Clip. This file includes the CAs or all referenced BLOBs and associated metadata. Metadata includes characteristics of CAS objects such as size, format and expiry date. 2 Marks Client present the data to be archived to the CAS API. The application server may also interact directly with the source like X-ray m/c API seperates the BLOB from the from meta data and CA is calculated from object’s binary representation. CA and metadata of the object are then inserted into the C-Clip DF. The C-Clip is then transferred to CAS. 3 Marks

questions.question: o Two technologies adopted for local replication are o Two technologies adopted for local replication are Host based Storage array based Host based Logical Volume Manager (LVM) based mirroring File System Snapshot Storage Array based Full volume mirroring Pointer based full volume replication Pointer based virtual replication 2 Marks o File System (FS) Snapshot is a Pointer-based replica Uses Copy on First Write (CoFW)principle When snapshot is created, bitmap and block map are created in metadata Bitmap: Used to track blocks that have changed on the production/source FS after creation of snap - initially all zero Block map: Used to indicate block address from which data is to be read when the data is accessed from the Snap FS - initially points to production/source FS Requires a fraction of the space used by the original FS Implemented by either FS itself or by LVM To read from snap FS, the bitmap is consulted. If 0, then the read is directed to the production FS. Read from production FS works as normal. If the bit is 1, then the block address is got from the block map and data is read from that address. 3 Marks
